column2: A hooded man in midnight blue pushed a book without a title into my hands. He said something, but it was lost in the crowd, and then he was gone. The book was still there.
Hey... wait!
Long study of the book will follow.
It wants me to read it...
The book is gibberish, and yet it enlightens me. Some chapters defeat me, but its mystery still holds me fast. Something is hidden in its language, and I mean to find out what.
The secret will soon be mine! Muhahaha... *cough* *cough*
The book's secret eludes me...
The book will be studied to the last page.

After weeks of study, wasted time and wasted ink, the 'secret' of the book still eluded me. The man must have been a madman, filling good parchment with nonsense and meaningless symbols. And yet I have come to love the hours in the library.
I learned to love books instead.
It took me weeks before the book gave up its first secret. The gibberish was a cipher, and after many sleepless nights I broke it and made a key. What I can read now only opens onto deeper mysteries.
The mystery is still not solved...
A nettlesome neighbour keeps sending me envoys, begging for gold one day and demanding tribute the next. His whims confuse me, and I am not sure what I should do.
I will send him roses.
Nail the envoys' hats to their heads!
My nettlesome neighbour has been very quiet since I sent his envoys home with their hats nailed to their heads.
Go me!
I wonder what happens if I do it like this...
A new punishment has been conceived.
Not many days after his astonished envoys came home, a letter arrived from my nettlesome neighbour. He was most grateful, and deeply touched by the red roses.
I told you so!
The roses finally came to good use.
The apple of [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s eye.
'Atone for thy sins!'\n\nMy subjects hate the new punishment of impalement. Led by the [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s, they show their outrage by pelting me with rotten vegetables!
'More! More!'\n\nMy subjects cannot get enough of the new punishment of impalement. Crowds gather at every stake. Only my steward complains, about the cost of the timber and the smell.
Vegetables won't stop me!
Maybe I should grow more roses?
The respect I won by nailing hats to envoys' heads has whetted my appetite. I have sent for a skilled torturer to teach me more about the stake.
More! More!
I'm having fun with it, for now.
My garden is the apple of my eye, my pride and joy. I do not trust my gardener, and I would spend every hour of the day among the roses if I could.
If I could, I would spend all my time in the garden.
I love my garden, but there are other things in life too.
My eager courtship of a certain lady, [target_courtier.GetFirstName], has got me nowhere. Her icy replies could cool the warmest heart. But I will not give up. There must be some way to win her.
Poetry could work!
My icy lady does not thaw...
Her heart has melted...
I will perform heroic deeds of valour!
The heroic deeds leave her cold...
The heroic deeds have won the icy lady!
My attempts to win her have come to nothing. She is as cold as Ulric's winter.
Forget it.
I won't give up!
I struggled with the poem for days, and sent it to her with a trembling heart. Her answer was warm and lovely. It seems the ice princess has thawed at last.
Words can't describe my feelings!

I never told my heart's desire that I would win her with deeds of valour, but soon I saw her at every tournament and every duel I fought. She began to smile at me, and laughed when I beat my opponents in her name.
Her heart has thawed for me!
The greatest tournament in years is to be held not far from here. The small victories I have won for my lady seem trivial now. I must win this one, so that she will love me forever.
My best will not be enough. I must win!
And the winner is...
With every poem I send her, a bigger piece of her heart is mine. I have chosen the ones we both love best and given them to the scribes to be copied out and illuminated properly.
I hope she will like it.
The book of poems.
The great tournament is over, and I alone am the victor. I could hardly believe it when the lady of my heart kissed me chastely on the cheek.
I love my life!
Can I stop doing this now?

I was mortified, then furious, when the scribe told me they liked my poems so much that they had made copies and sold them. The lady of my heart did not seem to care. She kissed me sweetly, thanked me, and said she already had a copy.
I should be furious, but I am just happy.
This is too humiliating!
My duties bore me, my courtiers bore me, everything bores me! I need something new and exciting in my life.
Some hunting will cheer me up.
A disastrous hunt.
A fortunate hunt.
Perhaps I should send for a new bird...
Disastrous falconry.
Fortunate falconry.
The hunt was a great disappointment. No game in sight, and my horse threw me.
Forget it.
I should try falconry instead.
We set out early, with the sun barely over the hills. There was game everywhere. The dogs caught many hares, and I slew a great boar before it could gut my horse.
We set out early, with the sun barely over the dunes. Game was plentiful, and no hunter rode home without a hare or a fowl tied to his saddle.
This day has been great!
The new bird had not been trained properly. It attacked one of the hounds and had to be killed before it let go of the poor, howling beast.
Now what?
I'll try hunting instead.
Hare after hare, my new bird caught them, killed them and brought them to me.
I like this.
I feel more at ease now. I can see to my duties and talk with my courtiers without being bored to tears. Perhaps I should hunt more often?
Yes!
I'm good for now.
The new bird is almost too perfect. I enjoy every hunt with her, and the cook is running out of recipes for hare.
I'm a falconer!
No more hare pie, please!
A new bird has arrived in the mews, and a new book on the art of poetry in the library.
I should start reading the book.
A book full of nonsense...
A book full of inspiration!
I should take her out hunting.
This book of poetry is deadly dull. It is all rules and more rules, and I want to throw it out of the window.
This wasn't for me.
I should take the bird out hunting instead.
The book of poetry is truly inspiring! I can feel the words bursting out of me.
Give me a quill!
The new bird is wilder than the ones I know. It killed many hares but would not give up its catch, and it even went for me when I tried to take one!
She is far too dangerous.
Poetry is safer. Let's try that instead.
My modest verses were never meant to be heard by anyone, yet wherever I go, bards and minstrels are reciting and singing them.
Fame and fortune await!
My poetry was never meant for others!
The priests preach restraint, while my friends try to tempt me with the pleasures of life. I cannot decide whether to enjoy this life or to deny myself for the gods' favour...
I can try a few pleasures...
I hope restraint won't bore me too much.
A waste of gold and a waste of time, but oh, how good it felt! The pleasures of life make everything less tiresome and more... delightful!
Sweet temptation...
Stay strong!
The first days were bearable, but then I began to notice every pretty face, and envied those who could indulge in sinful pleasures.
This is too hard!
I will stay strong!
The very thought of celibacy makes me shiver, and yet something is missing from my life. What is this emptiness inside me?
I need a few days to think about this.
Celibacy.
Ignore it, and live!
Hedonism.
Temptation is everywhere! The inviting glances, the lush bodies, the heady perfumes...
No! I will not give in!
Free! Free at last!
After a long, long, long time, I feel I could bear to live in perfect celibacy for the rest of my days.
Let's do it!
Maybe later.
This life of utmost pleasure suits me perfectly. The priests mutter about the Dark Prince and the road to ruin. Let them mutter.
More... more of everything!
I should think on this some more.

The pleasures of this life, or the rewards that Ormazd promises the faithful? Everything one longs for here will be waiting beyond. But life should not be dull, without flavour or delight! A true dilemma...
I live for the moment.
I will find true beauty and pleasure in poetry instead.
Rich food, sweet wine and good company. This life of pleasure makes me forget the grey world outside, and I indulge in everything...
...but I feel empty inside. There is no creativity in pleasure.
This is the life for me!
has decided what [Root.GetHerHis] life will be.
I have had enough. This life is not for me.
There is inspiration in everything, from the breakfast I devour to the sunlight on the flowers of my garden, from the old desert odes to the love songs of the Lashiek corsairs.
I have tired of this! Let me enjoy the pleasures of life instead.
I have found my calling.
Poetry speaks to [Root.GetTitledFirstName] as nothing else ever has.
Poetry is pleasant, but perhaps I will find something better.
It is the greatest decision of my life. I truly love the pleasures this life brings me, and its one rule, to do what pleases me most, is a rule I gladly follow.
I am a hedonist.
Pleasure is not a life I want to pursue for ever...
The life of a poet awaits me, if I truly believe it is the life for me. Reading and writing verse, I have learned more about my people's traditions and ways than ever before.
I am a poet!
Poetry is not a life I want to pursue for ever...

An Ormazdic Jurist knows the rulings of the law on every deed of man, and the evidence behind each one. The greatest Jurists of [Root.Location.GetName] have asked whether I would study with them, so that one day I might be counted among the great jurists of the faith.
This is a chance I dare not refuse.
It sounds like an awful lot of work... No, thank you.

A year of studying the law of Ormazd has left my head weary. The other Jurists are merciless. I must master the Scriptures, the Books of Justice and the Sacred Truth before the last examination, and only then may I call myself a Jurist.
I cannot quit now, so close to becoming a Jurist...
I give up. This is not the life I want...

At last I am a master of the law of Ormazd! My knowledge of the Scriptures, the Books of Justice and the Sacred Truth makes me a Jurist, and I will use it to be a better [Root.GetTitle] and ruler of my people.
I am proud to have become a Jurist!
I will use the knowledge, but not the title.
Tasting the forbidden wine of pleasure
This character is trying a life of pleasure, against the counsel of the priests of Ormazd.
Making the world more poetic
This character is trying the life of a poet.
